headline: Highest risk is medium: Great Expectations can read shared files and validate data, while the awesome-list agent is non-runnable and network-isolated, limiting pairwise harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot ingest B’s outputs by default. B can read files and produce validation results, but there is no documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or file handoff, which is unusual and low blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B's validation output into A-related tooling, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, B's file content can influence downstream prompts.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting B output into any prompt-driven workflow.
Disable shared clipboard between environments.
Review any file-to-prompt automation before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for any future shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches data sources, validation results, and documentation, but both agents have network_egress set to none, so exfiltration to a third party is not indicated. A touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces. The pair can still leak locally if files are shared, but the blast radius is limited and no default upload path is shown.
conditions: IF A and B are placed on the same shared filesystem, B's validation artifacts may be readable by A-side processes.
IF operators store sensitive data in B's data sources, those files can be exposed locally through shared access.
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions.
Store sensitive inputs outside any shared workspace.
Rotate or redact validation outputs before sharing.
Confirm both agents remain network-isolated.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities documented, so it cannot conflict on mutable resources. B can install packages and read/write files, but only its file surface is documented; there is no evidence of shared writable state with A. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration or a shared directory, so the risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, B may overwrite files used by another process.
IF package installation occurs in a shared environment, B can perturb the runtime state for adjacent jobs.
mitigations: Run B in an isolated virtualenv or container.
Keep A and B off the same writable path.
Pin package versions before installing.
Check for shared temp directories.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or workspace locks for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B produces validation results and documentation that downstream users may treat as authoritative, while A is a non-runnable reference list with no output channel. There is no direct evidence that B consumes A, but if A-derived recommendations are copied into B workflows, errors can cascade into incorrect validation or documentation decisions. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A-derived guidance is manually inserted into B's documentation or validation setup, B may act on unverified assumptions.
IF B's validation results are used as authoritative without review, downstream decisions can inherit errors.
mitigations: Require human review of any A-derived guidance before use.
Label B outputs as provisional until checked.
Keep source links alongside validation artifacts.
Add a second reviewer for changes based on B results.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both are network-isolated. B does handle validation results and documentation, so retention or residency issues could arise if operators place regulated data there, but that is not shown in the profiles. A has no relevant compliance surface, so only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in B's validation inputs or outputs, retention policy mismatches may matter.
IF operators require residency controls for documentation artifacts, B's file handling must be reviewed.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B unless policy is confirmed.
Document retention for validation artifacts.
Redact sensitive fields before validation.
Check residency requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
